Shakti Sagar And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18
April, 2023
Author: Samit Gopal

Bench: Samit Gopal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 71
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 7378 of 2023
Applicant :- Shakti Sagar And 4 Others

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :-

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J.

2. Heard Sri Deepak, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri U.P. Singh, learned counsel for the State and perused the records.
3.
Supplementary affidavit on behalf of the applicants filed today which is taken on record.

4. The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicants Shakti Sagar,
Virendra Pal Singh, Smt. Sarda Devi, Suresh Pal Singh, Smt. Reetu Devi with the prayer to quash the entire proceedings of Criminal Case and charge sheet dated 1.9.2020 as well as summoning order dated 10.3.2021 in Criminal Case No. 1742 of 2021, State vs. Shakti Sagar and others, arising out of Case Crime No. 332 of 2020, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act,
Shakti Sagar And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71014818/
1 P.S.- Hapur Dehat, District Hapur, pending in the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Hapur on the basis of compromise and with the further prayer to stay the further proceedings of the said case.
5.

entities.text: Shakti Sagar And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants argued that the parties have settled the dispute amicably out of court and on the basis of compromise the applicants filed the present Criminal Misc. Application U/S 482 Cr.P.C. before this Court in which an order for verification of the compromise was passed on 28.2.2023.

It is argued that in compliance of the order dated 28.2.2023 of this Court, the parties have filed the compromise before the trial court concerned for its verification after which the concerned court has verified the said compromise vide its order dated 28.3.2023, copy of the said order is annexure no. 1 to the supplementary affidavit dated 17.4.2023.

It is argued that the opposite party no. 2 is not interested to pursue the matter pending in the trial court and is not inclined to give any evidence against the applicants and therefore the impugned proceedings be quashed on the ground of compromise between the parties.
6.

Learned State counsel opposed the prayer for quashing but could not dispute the fact that the matter has been amicably settled between the parties which was duly verified by the concerned trial court.

7. The law with regards to quashing of a case on the basis of settlement arrived between the parties,
is well settled.

The Apex Court in the cases of (1) B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another: (2003)4 SCC 675; (2) Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation : (2008) 9 SCC 677; (3) Manoj Sharma Vs. State and others: ( 2008) 16 SCC 1; (4) Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab:
(2012) 10 SCC 303; (5) Shaifullah and others Vs. State of U.P. And another: 2013 (83) ACC 278 and (6) Parbatbhai Ahir@Parbatbhai @ Bhimsinbhai Karmur and others Vs. State of Gujarat and another: (2017) 9 SCC 641 has held that the cases in which the parties have settled their grievances can be quashed.

sentences.text:
8. From perusal of the records and the law laid down by the Apex Court on the subject matter, the present case is a good case for exercising powers by this Court to quash the proceedings/summoning order/charge sheet as prayed for by the applicant(s).
9.
10. The entire proceedings of said criminal case and charge sheet dated 1.9.2020 as well as summoning order dated 10.3.2021 are hereby quashed.
